newsitem.title: USA: British nanny indicted on first degree murder.
newsitem.headline: British nanny indicted on first degree murder.

text.p: A grand jury indicted an 18-year-old British nanny on a first degree murder charge on Wednesday in the death of a nine-month-old boy in her care, according to officials.

Louise Woodward, of Chester, England, has already been indicted on a charge of assault and battery in the February death of Matthew Eappen, and has pleaded not guilty to that charge. She is expected to enter a plea on the first degree murder charge in a Cambridge, Massachusetts, court on Friday, the Middlesex County District Attorney's office said.

A Middlesex County grand jury alleged that Woodward, who came to the United States in June 1996, caused the infant's death by severely shaking him and then striking his head on a hard surface, causing a skull fracture.

Woodward called rescue workers to her employer's home in the upscale neighbourhood of Newton, Massachusetts, on February 5 and told them that Eappen suddenly stopped breathing after being sick all day.
Eappen was on life support for four days before he died of a brain haemorrhage on February 9. Autopsy reports ruled the cause of death was a blunt blow to the head.
If convicted of first degree murder, Woodward would face a mandatory sentence of life in state prison with no parole eligibility, according to the Middlesex County District Attorney's office.
